preamble: Devoicing of the palatalized voiced stop [dʲ] to [tʲ] keeps the secondary palatal articulation while neutralizing voicing. It is best documented in Russian, where obstruents are devoiced word-finally and before voiceless obstruents, so /dʲ/ surfaces as [tʲ] and contrasts with the voiced form only before a vowel or sonorant. Neighbouring East Slavic languages do not share it: Belarusian has affricated /dʲ/ to [dzʲ] (dzekanne) and Ukrainian lacks final devoicing.

examples.note: Word-final devoicing of the palatalized dental stop; the soft sign keeps the palatalization.
Final [tʲ] alternates with voiced [dʲ] before a vowel, as in genitive груди́.
Regressive devoicing before voiceless [tʲ]; cf. singular будь with final [tʲ] and the voiced stem in буду 'I will be'.

sources: Wikipedia contributors (2026). Russian phonology: Final devoicing. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Russian_phonology
